messages.author: ce16cbb0a05ab2b1
messages.subject: isolating double recombinants in individuals
parts:
Karl,
Is there way to simply identify double cross-over events?  I am looking for possible genotyping errors (using a high-throughput genotyping pipeline).  Many times errors can be found by checking all of the double recombination events.  If a single marker for an individual is typed as A when all of the surrounding genotypes are B, this double crossover event may represent a genotyping error.

top.errorlod and plot.geno locate some potential genotyping errors, but I would like to parse my data for all double recombination events surrounding a single marker.

I can use locateXO to find the estimated locations of recombination events.  Is there a straightforward way in R to check to see if these locations surround, say, a single marker?  I can think of some ways to do it that involve several levels of looping over marker intervals, but I was hoping that there might be a simpler way to do this.

Any ideas?

Thanks!
Kevin

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] isolating double recombinants in individuals
parts:
The locateXO() function, particularly with the argument full.info=TRUE, is the best we have.

karl
